decisions.statement: A world is built once and copied for each test that asks for that world.
Git packs nothing in that world on its own.
A page's file is named for the page type that page states.
A page put into a world writes the shapes beside that page's page type.
A world's shapes are composed from every page put into it so far.
A shapes file the world did not write is left as whatever wrote it left it.
A page arriving beside a shapes file already there has its own shape merged in.
A shape no page arriving carries is left, so a shape a settle took away stays away.
A world's commit holds the shapes the pages in that commit imply.
A change's code is reached from the akasha folder above rather than by folders counted up.
Moving this module leaves where that folder is found the same.
That folder is found by walking up rather than by a package name.
A world built under a test overlay resolves no package name of its own.

definition: the world of pages a test is set up with
